goldens.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:93 — With FGAP V1 flag enabled alongside V2, the GroupRemovedEvent listener now reaches GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled which throws UnsupportedOperationException, failing group deletion (cascade failure).

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissions.registerListener(), the GroupRemovedEvent handler unconditionally calls `management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getGroup(), false)`. This diff introduces `MgmtPermissionsV2.groups()` returning `GroupPermissionsV2`, and `GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...)` is implemented to throw `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. Therefore, when the listener runs in a V2 permissions context, a group removal event would trigger this UnsupportedOperationException, plausibly breaking group deletion/cascade cleanup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:123 — V2 getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authz resource IDs (not group IDs, which are the resource names) and findByType("Groups") won't match untyped per-group resources, so UserModel.GROUPS filter in users search/count endpoints receives wrong IDs

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, the code iterates `resourceStore.findByType(..., GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, groupResource -> ...)` and then passes `groupResource.getId()` into `hasPermission(...)` and also adds `groupResource.getId()` to the returned set. But `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)` looks up resources by *name* (`resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`), implying the identifier it expects is the group ID used as the resource name (as also suggested by the non-V2 implementation adding `resource.getName()`). Using the authz resource internal ID will typically fail the name lookup and/or return a set of non-group IDs, which then gets stored into `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` in users search/count paths, breaking filtering based on group IDs.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:147 — Public interface method getGroupsWithViewPermission() renamed and getGroupsWithViewPermission(GroupModel) removed without deprecation shim, breaking extension callers

While internal usages are updated (e.g., `UsersResource` now calls `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`), any external implementers/callers of this public interface would break at compile time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/utils/ModelToRepresentation.java:175 — Public static searchGroupModelsByAttributes removed from server-spi-private without deprecation, breaking external callers

While internal usages in this PR are updated (e.g., `GroupsResource` now calls `session.groups().searchGroupsByAttributes(...)` directly), the removal of a public method is a source/binary compatibility break for any downstream code that called it. The diff does not show any deprecation period or replacement shim, so the compatibility concern is real, though the claim about specific “external callers” cannot be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:328 — getResourceName not extended for Groups type, so permission REST responses show raw group-ID resource names instead of group names/"All groups"

In `getOrCreateResource(...)`, the computed `name` is used when creating the authorization `Resource`, so group permission resources will be named by raw group ID. That matches the finding’s concern about REST responses/UX showing IDs rather than group names (though the diff doesn’t show a `getResourceName` method specifically).

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:120 — getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses findByType("Groups"), which matches only the type resource (per-group resources get no type), then adds resource.getId() (authz UUID, not group id) and looks it up via findByName; per-group view-members grants are ignored and a bogus id is put in UserModel.GROUPS.

adjudication.rationale: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the callback iterates resources found by type and then calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and, on success, adds groupResource.getId() to the returned set. But hasPermission(String groupId, ...) treats its argument as a *group id/resource name* (it does resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)), while Resource.getId() is the authorization resource UUID (distinct from the resource name / group id). This means per-group permissions can be missed (findByName won’t locate the per-group resource when given the authz UUID) and the returned Set<String> can contain authz resource IDs rather than realm group IDs, which is then stored into session attribute UserModel.GROUPS in UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource, leading to incorrect user filtering/visibility.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:121 — getGroupIdsWithViewPermission mixes up ID types: per-group resources are untyped (named by group id), so findByType only matches the "Groups" type resource, and its resource id (not a group id) goes into the "group IDs" set.

adjudication.rationale: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), it iterates resources via resourceStore.findByType(..., GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, groupResource -> ...) but then uses groupResource.getId() both to call hasPermission(...) and to add into the returned “group IDs” set. However, hasPermission(String groupId, ...) treats the argument as a *group id used as the resource name* (resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)). Passing Resource.getId() (the authorization resource’s internal id) will typically not match the resource name (group id), causing findByName to return null and triggering fallback to the type-level resource ("all-groups"), and the returned set will contain authorization resource ids rather than group ids. This directly contradicts the method contract and breaks the filtering behavior that now relies on group IDs (e.g., UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource set UserModel.GROUPS to this set).

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:65 — canManage() also passes on the VIEW scope, so view-only access counts as manage (the javadoc at GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:78 documents the same mistake).

adjudication.rationale: In the new `GroupPermissionsV2` implementation, `canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, meaning a caller granted only the `VIEW` scope (e.g., via an all-groups permission) would be treated as able to “manage” groups. This is inconsistent with the non-V2 behavior (`GroupPermissions.canManage()` requires `AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS`) and would allow manage-gated operations to succeed with view-only permissions. The Javadoc added in `GroupPermissionEvaluator` also reflects this same incorrect semantics (“VIEW or MANAGE groups” for `canManage()`), reinforcing that the diff introduces/exposes this as a real authorization bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:135 — The requireManageMembers javadoc cites canManageMembership, but the implementation calls canManageMembers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a Javadoc inconsistency in `GroupPermissionEvaluator`: `requireManageMembers(GroupModel group)` is documented as throwing if `canManageMembership(group)` is false, while by naming/intent it should refer to `canManageMembers(group)`. This is a documentation/style issue only; no implementation change or behavioral defect is shown in this interface diff (interfaces don’t “call” anything here).

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:145 — The javadoc says "@return Stream of IDs", but the method returns a Set.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a Javadoc/signature mismatch: the comment above `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` says "@return Stream of IDs" while the method returns `Set<String>`. However this is a documentation nit and not a verifiable behavioral/correctness defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:130 — The private hasPermission is a near-copy of UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission (same all-resource fallback and scope loop) and should be a shared helper.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `GroupPermissionsV2` with a private `hasPermission(String groupId, String... scopes)` that implements the same pattern seen in `UserPermissionsV2` (resource-specific lookup, fallback to an all-resource-type resource when specific resource is absent, then iterating evaluated permissions’ scopes to match expected scopes). This is a concrete duplication created by the change (new file) and is a maintainability/architecture issue rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:83 — GroupPermissionsV2 extends V1 GroupPermissions only to throw UnsupportedOperationException from 9 management methods, and the V1 fields were made protected just for it; this inheritance breaks Liskov substitution and couples V2 to V1 internals.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `GroupPermissionsV2 extends GroupPermissions` and overrides multiple management-oriented methods to `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")` (e.g., `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `viewMembersPermission`, `manageMembersPermission`, `manageMembershipPermission`, `viewPermission`, `managePermission`, `resource`, `getPermissions`). It also changes `GroupPermissions` fields (`root`, `resourceStore`, `policyStore`) from `private` to `protected`, which appears motivated by subclass access. This is a concrete design/architecture concern introduced by the change (V2 coupled to V1 internals and exposing runtime exceptions via inherited API), but the diff alone does not prove these methods are invoked in V2 paths to cause an immediate functional failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/UserPermissionEvaluator.java:164 — isImpersonatable is marked @Deprecated with no javadoc or replacement pointer, although a replacement exists (canImpersonate(user, requester)).

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `UserPermissionEvaluator` adds `@Deprecated boolean isImpersonatable(UserModel user, ClientModel requester);` near the end with no accompanying Javadoc explaining deprecation or pointing to a replacement, while the interface otherwise adds detailed Javadocs and `canImpersonate(UserModel, ClientModel)` remains present and documented. This is a real, diff-grounded documentation/API clarity issue but not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/GroupsResource.java:113 — Removed once-per-request canViewGlobal short-circuit; under V2 GroupPermissionsV2.canView(group) has no type-level check, so an admin with all-groups VIEW triggers a full per-group policy evaluation (N+1) for every listed group.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsResource.getGroups`, the diff replaces `boolean canViewGlobal = groupsEvaluator.canView(); ... filter(g -> canViewGlobal || groupsEvaluator.canView(g))` with `stream.filter(groupsEvaluator::canView)`. Under the new V2 implementation (`GroupPermissionsV2.canView(GroupModel)`), non-role-based access calls `hasPermission(group.getId(), ...)`, which evaluates authorization (potentially falling back to the type-level “all-groups” resource when the per-group resource is missing). Regardless of that fallback, the filter now triggers a permission evaluation per group in the stream, whereas previously a single `canView()` result could short-circuit the per-group checks for globally-authorized admins. This is a diff-grounded performance regression (N evaluations for N groups), not a functional correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/GroupResource.java:179 — getSubGroupsStream(-1,-1) materializes all subgroups and now runs a per-group V2 permission evaluation on each (no global short-circuit) before in-memory pagination, making cost O(all children) evaluations per page.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupResource.getSubGroups`, the stream source is still `group.getSubGroupsStream(search, exact, -1, -1)`, i.e., not server-paginated, and results are paginated via `paginatedStream(...)` afterwards. The diff removes the prior global short-circuit (`boolean canViewGlobal = auth.groups().canView(); ... filter(g -> canViewGlobal || auth.groups().canView(g))`) and replaces it with `filter(auth.groups()::canView)`, which forces a per-subgroup permission check even when the caller has global view. With V2 `GroupPermissionsV2.canView(GroupModel)` potentially doing scope-based evaluation, this can increase per-page cost to scanning/evaluating many children before enough pass the filter for pagination. This is a concrete performance/regression concern shown by the diff, not a functional correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:141 — hasPermission issues findByName plus, when no per-group resource exists, policyStore.findByResource on the type resource for every group checked, adding repeated DB queries per group instead of caching the all-groups result.

adjudication.rationale: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), it iterates authorization Resources via resourceStore.findByType(..., groupResource -> { if (hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)) ... }). But hasPermission(String groupId, ...) treats its argument as a *group id/name* and does resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId). Passing Resource.getId() (typically an internal UUID) will likely not match the resource name (elsewhere the code uses group.getId() as the resource name), so resource lookup returns null and the method falls back to the type resource ("all-groups") and calls policyStore.findByResource(...) for each group iteration. This both breaks per-group permission evaluation and causes repeated DB queries per group, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:70 — V2 groups canManage() accepts the VIEW scope, so an admin with only all-groups view permission passes requireManage() in GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup and can create top-level groups or move any existing group (by id) to top level (privilege escalation).

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `GroupPermissionsV2`, `canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, i.e., it treats the VIEW scope as sufficient for “manage” at the resource-type (all-groups) level. Because `requireManage()` in `GroupPermissions` delegates to `canManage()`, any call site using `auth.groups().requireManage()` (for collection-level mutations like creating groups) would be satisfied by an admin granted only all-groups VIEW permission. This is an over-permissive authorization check and can enable privilege escalation depending on how `requireManage()` is used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:123 — V2 getGroupIdsWithViewPermission passes and collects the authz resource UUID (groupResource.getId()) instead of the group id (resource name), so per-group view-members grants are evaluated against the wrong resource and the UserModel.GROUPS search filter gets non-group ids, which drifts from V1 behavior.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionsV2#getGroupIdsWithViewPermission`, the code iterates `resourceStore.findByType(..., groupResource -> { ... })` and calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` and, on success, adds `groupResource.getId()` to the returned set. However, `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)` treats its argument as a *group id / resource name* by doing `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`. Passing the authz resource UUID (`groupResource.getId()`) will typically fail `findByName`, causing the method to fall back to the resource-type (“all-groups”) resource and thereby mis-evaluate per-group grants. Additionally, returning authz resource UUIDs in the set will mismatch the expected group-id semantics when callers set `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` (e.g., in `UsersResource`/`BruteForceUsersResource`), likely breaking group-filtered user search behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:121 — getGroupIdsWithViewPermission looks up and returns authz resource IDs instead of group IDs, so it never matches per-group permissions; the view-members tests only pass through the post-filter fallback, and users count() and paginated search are never tested

adjudication.rationale: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the code iterates authz Resources by type and adds groupResource.getId() to the returned set, and also passes groupResource.getId() into hasPermission(). But hasPermission(String groupId, ...) treats its argument as a *group ID/name* and does resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId). For group resources, the schema resolves the group resource name via resolveGroup() to group.getId() (i.e., the group ID as the resource *name*), while the authz Resource internal id is typically different. Using resource.getId() therefore won’t match findByName(), causing per-group permissions to be missed and returning/using the wrong identifiers in places that expect actual group IDs (e.g., session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds) in UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource).

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:70 — canManage() returns true on the VIEW scope, and no test checks that a view-only admin is still blocked from manage operations such as creating top-level groups

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` returning `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` (i.e., VIEW alone can satisfy a method named `canManage`) while `canManage(GroupModel)` requires MANAGE. This is a concrete, reviewable concern about potentially over-broad authorization semantics introduced in the diff. Also, the newly added tests (e.g., `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest`) verify create-group behavior with `MANAGE` but do not include a negative test asserting that an admin granted only `VIEW` on groups still cannot perform manage operations like creating top-level groups, so the test gap is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java:306 — testManageGroupMembership never checks that bob actually joined the group, and never checks that manage-membership alone (without the user-side permission) or a different group is denied

MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP)`) and never exercises the newly introduced authorization logic with negative cases (e.g., group MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP without the user-side MANAGE_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP, or permission on a different group). adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java:91 — No test covers subgroup inheritance of view-members/manage-members, deny (negative) policies, or a per-group deny overriding an all-groups grant

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces nontrivial new authz logic for group resource type evaluation in `GroupPermissionsV2` (e.g., `hasPermission()` fallback to the all-groups resource type when a per-group `Resource` is missing, and scope checks for `VIEW_MEMBERS`/`MANAGE_MEMBERS`), plus hierarchical evaluation for users via group membership (`UserPermissions.canViewByGroup()` now uses `root.groups()::canViewMembers`). The newly added `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest` covers basic positive cases (granting `VIEW_MEMBERS`/`MANAGE_MEMBERS`, `VIEW`/`MANAGE`, and all-groups grants), but it does not exercise edge cases implied by the new logic, such as subgroup/parent inheritance scenarios in the group chain or policy conflict/override behavior (e.g., per-group restrictions vs an all-groups grant). Given the added fallback/precedence behavior in `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission()`, the absence of tests for these cases is a specific, diff-grounded review gap rather than a generic “add more tests” request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissions.java:340 — V1 behavior changed (canViewMembers now accepts manage-members; getGroupIdsWithViewPermission no longer short-circuits on users().canManage(); canList/canView rewritten) but no V1 regression tests were added

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change V1 permission-evaluator logic in `GroupPermissions` (e.g., `canViewMembers` now treats `MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE` as sufficient: `hasPermission(group, VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE, MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE)`, `getGroupsWithViewPermission(...)` was removed and replaced with `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` with different short-circuiting, and `canList/canView/canManage` were rewritten to use role checks directly). The only added tests are `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest` under `tests/.../authz/fgap/` and related config updates, which exercise the new V2 resource-type/scopes behavior (AdminPermissionsSchema-based), not V1 `GroupPermissions` behavior. So the finding about missing V1 regression coverage for these V1 behavior changes is specific and supported by the diff, but it is a testing/coverage concern rather than a directly verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/UserPermissionsV2.java:645 — canMapRoles and canManageGroupMembership now also grant via the user MANAGE scope and group manage-members, but no test covers these new paths

adjudication.rationale:
In the diff, `UserPermissionsV2.canMapRoles` and `canManageGroupMembership` were broadened to allow access via the user `MANAGE` scope and via `canManageByGroup(user)` (which evaluates group-chain permissions, ultimately tied to group member-management scopes). Concretely:
- `canMapRoles`: now `hasPermission(..., MANAGE, MAP_ROLES) || canManageByGroup(user)`
- `canManageGroupMembership`: now `hasPermission(..., MANAGE, MANAGE_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP) || canManageByGroup(user)`
The newly added test `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest` exercises viewing/managing users via `VIEW_MEMBERS`/`MANAGE_MEMBERS` and group membership management via `MANAGE_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP` + `MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP`, but it does not cover the specific new paths for (a) granting map-roles/group-membership management via the user-level `MANAGE` scope, nor (b) the group-chain `canManageByGroup` fallback for these two methods. The diff does not show any other added/updated tests targeting these new branches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java:280 — The all-groups view assertion only checks the count (hasSize 2), not which groups came back, and never tests subgroup listing filtered through GroupResource.getSubGroups

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:74 — The listener is now registered only if the feature is enabled at registration time (previously checked per event), and no test covers the group/role removal cleanup

adjudication.rationale: The diff in AdminPermissions.registerListener changes behavior from always registering a listener and gating logic per-event (previously: listener registered unconditionally, then `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(...)) { ... }` inside `onEvent`) to only registering the listener when the feature is enabled at registration time (`if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(...)) { manager.register(...) }`). This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral change that could matter if feature enablement were to differ between registration time and event time (even if that’s uncommon). Also, the added tests in this PR (e.g., GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest) cover permission evaluation paths, but there is no new test exercising the listener cleanup behavior on role/group removal events, so the “no test covers cleanup” part is consistent with what’s shown.
